visita.heroSubtitle: A place of history, art and spirituality open to all, on Praça da Estrela.
visita.historiaP1: The Basílica da Estrela is the most remarkable 18th-century monument in the city of Lisbon. It was commissioned by Queen Maria I and dedicated by her to the Most Holy Heart of Jesus in fulfilment of a vow — should she have an heir to succeed her on the throne.
visita.historiaP2: Construction of the Basílica, at Casal da Estrela, took 10 years (1779–1789). Its architects were Mateus Vicente de Oliveira and Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos, both of the Mafra School.
visita.historiaP3: Beside it, and earlier than the Basílica, the Queen had a Convent built for the Discalced Carmelites of Saint Teresa, from Carnide. Some have seen in the Basílica da Estrela an imitation of St Peter’s in Rome.
visita.conhecerText: Seven things worth seeking out, from the atrium to the facade.
visita.c1Desc: Entry is through an atrium (galilee) in which, set in niches, stand the statues of the Mother of Jesus and Saint Joseph, from the school of Joaquim Machado de Castro. To the left lies the Baptistery.
visita.c2Desc: The interior, clad in marbles of various colours from Pero Pinheiro, Sintra and Cascais, presents a spacious nave of great decorative effect. This nave and the transept are covered by a vault. The lining of the great dome is entirely in grey, pink and ochre marble. In it stand out the oculi and tall windows through which a golden light spreads across the Basílica. The harmony of the lines; the nobility of the materials used — marble, bronze, gilt woodwork; the columns, balustrades and galleries; the sculpted crownings with figures; the altarpieces; the confessionals and vestment chests; the frames and floral ornaments, carved by artists of the period, all contribute to the beauty of the temple.
visita.c3Desc: Almost all the paintings in the various chapels and the panel of the high altar were painted in Rome by Pompeo Batoni. The latter represents an allegory of the cult of the Heart of Jesus, painted in mid-heaven, among luminous clouds and surrounded by Cherubim and Seraphim in adoration. At the centre, a chalice with the Sacred Host and on either side two figures — the Church and Charity. Below, four figures represent Asia, Africa, America and Europe — the four parts of the World — in adoration of the Most Holy Heart. There are other canvases, one painted by the Infantas, representing the Sacred Heart of Mary and the Archangels, another, of Saint Anne teaching Our Lady to read, attributed to Pedro Alexandrino de Carvalho.
visita.c4Desc: In the transept, on the right-hand side, stands the tomb of the Foundress (1816). Also on this side can be seen the Tenebrae Candlestick, a work attributed to the carver José de Abreu de Ó (1790).
visita.c5Desc: The Nativity Scene of the Basílica da Estrela is the work of Machado de Castro and his disciples. Grand in conception, it gained fame for its beauty and for being one of the largest ever modelled. It is placed in a room behind the Queen’s tomb.
visita.c6Desc: In the sacristy can be seen the tomb of the Archbishop of Thessalonica, Friar Inácio de São Caetano, the Queen’s confessor, considered the second founder of the Convent and the Basílica. The sculpture at the centre of the tomb is by Machado de Castro. Beside the tomb, a beautiful marble lavabo. The vestment chests are attributed to the carver José de Abreu do Ó.
visita.c7Desc: The facade of the Basílica da Estrela is imposing, harmonious, ornamented with fine statuary executed by Joaquim Machado de Castro, his assistants and disciples. It is composed of three bodies, the central one crowned by a pediment. Above four columns rise, in the central body, the statues of Faith, Devotion, Gratitude and Liberality. The bas-relief adorning the frontage represents the adoration of the Most Holy Heart of Jesus. In niches, above, the images of the Prophet Elijah and Saint John of the Cross; below, Saint Teresa of Ávila and Saint Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi. Entry to the atrium is through three great wrought-iron gates. The bell towers are topped by carved spires adorned with baroque finials. In the lower part of the towers, the clock faces. The church is covered by a terrace. Above the crossing rises the majestic dome, crowned at the top by a lantern with a balcony all around. Above the lantern rises the sphere, topped by an iron cross.

visita.exp2Desc: A guided visit to one of the great works of Portuguese sculpture, with more than 500 figures in cork and terracotta.
visita.exp3Desc: Organ and choral music in the nave, making the most of the dome's acoustics at the end of the day.

celebracoes.heroSubtitle: Sacraments, liturgy and devotions — the gestures that shape the year and the life of a Christian community.
celebracoes.intro: From the daily Eucharist to devotions that span centuries, the Basílica keeps its own rhythm of prayer and celebration, open to those arriving for the first time and to those who have come for a lifetime.
celebracoes.sacramentosText: The seven sacraments accompany the stages of Christian life. All are celebrated at the Basílica, each with its own preparation.
celebracoes.sac1Desc: Entry into Christian life. Celebrated on Sundays, with prior preparation for parents and godparents.
celebracoes.sac2Desc: The centre of the Church's life, celebrated daily. First Communion is prepared through catechesis.
celebracoes.sac3Desc: Confirmation completes Christian initiation. Prepared in the youth groups, from 10th grade.
celebracoes.sac4Desc: The sacrament of reconciliation, available before celebrations and at set times.
celebracoes.sac5Desc: Comfort and strength in illness. May be requested at any time, including at home.
celebracoes.sac6Desc: Celebrated by appointment, following the preparation course for engaged couples.
celebracoes.sac7Desc: The sacrament of ordained ministry, in service of the community.
celebracoes.sacramentosNota: For bookings and preparation, please contact the parish office.
celebracoes.liturgiaText: The liturgical year gives shape to the community's time: Advent and Christmas, Lent and Easter, Ordinary Time. Each season has its colour, its music and its own way of praying.
celebracoes.liturgiaText2: At the Basílica, solemn celebrations mark the great feasts of the year, with particular emphasis on the solemnity of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, to whom the church is dedicated.
celebracoes.missasText: The Basílica celebrates the Eucharist daily. Times may change on solemnities.
celebracoes.intencoesText: You may ask for a Mass to be celebrated for a particular intention — for someone who has died, in thanksgiving, or for a personal request.
celebracoes.confissoesText: A priest is always available at the times listed. Outside them, an appointment can be arranged through the parish office.
celebracoes.devocoesText: Four devotions mark the Basílica's calendar. Each with its own history and its own promise.
celebracoes.adoracaoQuote: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
celebracoes.adoracaoText: To place oneself at the feet of Christ and recognise in Him the real presence that nourishes and transforms. A silent encounter, to offer Him one's heart, sorrows and intentions.
celebracoes.adoracaoClose: Jesus waits for us in this sacrament of love.
celebracoes.sextasQuote: To all those who receive Communion on the first Friday of nine consecutive months, I will grant the grace of final perseverance and eternal salvation.
celebracoes.sextasOrigem: 17th century, Paray-le-Monial. The Sacred Heart of Jesus reveals itself to Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque, promising special graces to those who receive Communion on the First Friday of nine consecutive months.
celebracoes.sextasBasilica: Adoration and Confessions from 18h to 19h. Mass follows at 19h, for the intentions of the Holy Father.
celebracoes.sabadosQuote: To all those who, on five consecutive first Saturdays, go to confession, receive Holy Communion, pray the rosary and keep Me company for fifteen minutes, I promise to assist them at the hour of death with all the graces necessary for salvation.
celebracoes.sabadosOrigem: Fátima, 1925. Our Lady appears to Sister Lúcia at Pontevedra and asks for an act of reparation in honour of her Immaculate Heart, promising the grace of final perseverance.
celebracoes.sabadosBasilica: Rosary, Confession, meditation on the mysteries and the Eucharist — in a spirit of reparation and offering to the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
celebracoes.sabadosClose: In the end, my Immaculate Heart will triumph.
celebracoes.tercoQuote: If you wish peace to reign in your families and in your country, pray the Holy Rosary together every day.
celebracoes.tercoText: Parents, children and grandparents before Our Lady, entrusting to her the life of the home and asking her protection.

donativos.heroSubtitle: The Basílica lives on the contribution of those who visit it, those who pray in it and those who want it standing for the generations to come.
donativos.intro: Keeping the Basílica open has a daily cost — the upkeep of the building, the liturgy, the social work among those most in need. Every donation sustains a part of that life.
donativos.modalidadesText: Each answers a different situation — from those passing through the Basílica once to those who have supported it for years. All lead to the same form, at the end of this page.
donativos.unicaDesc: A single donation, of any amount, made there and then. It is the simplest way to contribute.
donativos.periodicoDesc: A recurring contribution, monthly or yearly, giving the parish the predictability it needs to plan.
donativos.palavraDesc: A form of giving particular to this parish. The text for this section will be written with the parish.
donativos.obrasDesc: Giving towards a specific restoration project, rather than to the general fund.
donativos.geraisDesc: Undesignated: the parish applies it wherever the need is greatest at the time.
donativos.formNotasHelp: Optional — for example, the intention for which you are requesting the Mass.
donativos.formSeguranca: Payment is completed on Easypay. The Basílica neither receives nor stores your card details.
donativos.ctaSubtitle: For other kinds of donation, legacies or support for a specific project, the parish office will answer any questions.

vidaParoquia.heroSubtitle: Groups, movements, formation and culture — the parish happens every day of the week, not only on Sundays.
vidaParoquia.manifesto: The Basílica doesn't close its doors after Mass. Between catechesis, scouting, choir and formation, there's always something happening — faith lived in community, not only in silence.
vidaParoquia.gruposText: Each group has its own rhythm and mission. There's room for those who want to serve, learn, pray or simply be present.
vidaParoquia.grupo1Desc: Ages 6 to 16, meeting weekly on Tuesdays — through First Communion, the Profession of Faith and, from 10th grade, Confirmation preparation.
vidaParoquia.grupo2Desc: For secondary-school students, preparing for Confirmation and for an active, missionary Christian life.
vidaParoquia.grupo3Desc: Direct service at the altar and in the proclamation of the Word, at every celebration.
vidaParoquia.grupo4Desc: Moments of communal prayer through the week, outside the celebration schedule.
vidaParoquia.escuteirosText: The parish scout group and apostolic movements accompany children, young people and adults on a path of faith built on service, nature and friendship.
vidaParoquia.culturaisText: Music, heritage and culture have been part of the Basílica's life since its founding.
vidaParoquia.cultural1Desc: Singing and liturgical music at every Sunday celebration and solemnity.
vidaParoquia.cultural2Desc: Study, outreach and preservation of the Basílica's artistic collection.
vidaParoquia.cultural3Desc: A musical programme open to the city, throughout the liturgical year.
vidaParoquia.formacaoText: Formation cycles open to the whole community, with no prior registration required unless otherwise stated.
vidaParoquia.ctiText: A project dedicated to the parish's youngest members, with its own activities throughout the year.
vidaParoquia.reservasText: The parish rooms are available for meetings, formation sessions and parish group gatherings.
vidaParoquia.reserva2Desc: Request to the parish office at least one week in advance.
